chunks: Yahya al-Halabi, from Abu al-Mustahal, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked me: 'What invited you to the place where you placed Zayd?' I said: 'Three issues. As for one of them, there were few who were left behind with us; we were only eight persons. And as for the other, it was what we feared from the morning, that it would expose us. And as for the third, it was his bed (resting place) which he had proceeded to.' He said: 'How far is the Euphrates from the place in which you placed him?' I said: 'A stone's throw.'

He said: 'Glory be to Allah! Why did you not tie a piece of iron to him and throw him into the Euphrates, and that would have been preferable?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, no, by Allah, we had no way for this.' He said: 'What were you on the day you went out with Zayd?' I said: 'Believers.' He said: 'Who were your enemies?' I said: 'Infidels.'

For I find in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'O you who believe! When you meet those who disbelieve in battle, then smite their necks until, when you have overcome them, then make them prisoners, and thereafter either set them free as a favour or let them ransom (themselves) until the war lays down its burdens.'
You began by evacuating yourselves from captivity. Glory be to Allah! You did not have the ability to travel with justice even for a while.

key_terms.تَخْلِيَةِ مَنْ أَسَرْتُمْ: Evacuating/letting go of those you captured

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq criticize the burial of Zayd in the Euphrates narrative?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) critiques the companions' decision to bury Zayd on land, suggesting that throwing him into the Euphrates would have been a more profound act of justice, as the river is a public domain. He references Quran 47:4 to highlight that while the Quran permits freeing or ransoming prisoners of war, the companions' choice to bury him rather than dispose of him in a manner that maximized public benefit (like the Euphrates) was a missed opportunity to exercise 'adl (justice) in their conduct.
